缺点是有的而且很明显，怪、运送、配额、猫限时等机制每个层面都不深，很浅的结合造就了最短2小时的乐趣。 但价格也很低，性价比高，所以好评。 这套找东西——带回——赚钱——买物品的机制正反馈很强，新鲜时的体验相当好，比一些同价位的恐怖游戏强很多了。 不过新鲜期过后，在买到第三个通行证之前钱就多的没地方用了，能买的全买光，正反馈断掉。 这套玩法真的很适合做多周目或Rogue元素的。不过目前的体量就够2遍，第一遍摸索第二遍速通。 个人认为的建议： 增加怪的种类，并且给相应的道具应对。 比如某种怪会潜伏在货架上，玩家靠近会被定身，玩家可以用灯光驱逐。 比如某种怪会快速移动，不会攻击玩家，但会发出警报来吸引大头怪，玩家需要用某种道具来阻止其报警。 加入一些吸引怪或控制怪的道具，小闹钟灭火器之类，可以影响怪物走向或解围。 给主角一些后期很昂贵但强大的能力或道具，让玩家在资金充裕时获得额外体验，可以是仅限当天的消耗性能力。比如加速跑，万能钥匙，怪物透视仪。 加入头灯节省手电栏位，为其它道具留出空间。 货架加入Rogue随机，在后期玩家购买全部猫咪物品后时间非常充裕，用随机货架来延长寻找时间。 猫咪的玩法也过少，只有买加时长的道具而已，加入猫咪互动，比如猫可能会溜出屋子进入仓库，玩家需要限时将猫咪找回，奖励时长或金钱。 这样可以增加一些重复游玩的价值。

我，一名光荣的养猫人， 在此庄严宣誓： 无论贫穷还是富有， 无论忙碌还是悠闲， 我都将无条件爱我的猫， 做它最忠诚的铲屎官。 我承诺： 每天准时喂粮，绝不拖延； 定期清理猫砂，保持清新； 让它在我床上肆意打滚， 纵容它偶尔的任性与小脾气。 我发誓： 在它蹭我腿时，放下手机； 在它喵喵叫时，耐心回应； 在它闯祸时，默默收拾残局， 绝不责怪，因为它是我的主子。 我深知： 养猫不是一时兴起， 而是一辈子的责任与陪伴。 无论它掉毛多严重， 无论它抓坏多少家具， 我都将无怨无悔， 因为它是我生命中的光。 最后，我郑重宣告： 我的家，就是猫的领地； 我的心，就是猫的港湾。 从此以后， 猫好，我快乐； 猫坏，猫不可能坏！ 宣誓人：一名卑微的铲屎官 日期：今天，明天，以及未来的每一天！

To echo some other reviews, on the surface it was interesting but after the second day you quickly understand how bare the game is. The game only shows more of its flaws the further you progress. I ended up finishing the game in less than two hours, only died once, and did it in 9 days in the warehouse. Once I realized that there was really only one actual thing to watch out for on the warehouse floors, the game became a lot less scary. The game relies a lot on accenting things with horror stingers or environmental noise to generate scare factor, and you quicky learn that only the roaming enemy with a distinctive footstep can actually hurt you. This does not change even as you unlock other areas. The only monster just becomes more numerous or slightly changes appearance. Hiding spots from the monster are incredibly frequent, you have to actively put yourself in an awful position to ever be at risk of being caught. Squatting under a waist high crawlspace is more than enough to make the monster give up and walk away allowing you to immediately walk in the other direction as soon as he turns around, removing any potential threatening aura the monster had. The certificates to advance to areas with items that have higher payouts i've found are actually downgrades. A lot of the subsequent areas vastly increase the amount of running around you have to do without a matching increase in payout. The cat was a funny addition/motivator, but also very simple. There is no interactivity besides petting him and its boredom meter is an arbitrary time limit to how long you can spend outside your room. Packing things once you understand what to do is virtually impossible to mess up and formulaic. I was disappointed the cat doesn't even do anything but lounge at 4-5 pre-defined spots. There were a very surprising amount of what I thought were enemies but just turned out to be set pieces to scare you. Early on in the main warehouse you'll see a guy skittering on all fours as you walk down an aisle. Spooks you at first, but after the third time you realize he's not actually there and conveniently only shows up right in front of you. After the 10th time you just ignore him. The same goes for environmental noises. Every new area I unlocked I kept hoping "maybe they'll introduce the new enemy here", but a new enemy was never introduced. I will say that the game is polished. I don't think I actually encountered any bugs while playing. I just feel like the mechanics of the game were presented but not expanded upon. Nothing actually changes as you progress in collecting the items for packing besides unlocking upgrades that reduce how many trips you need. Keypad combinations don't become more or less difficult, finding the related rack and item does not change, and evading enemy detection doesn't change. I would have liked to see some changes in the game's formula or strategy instead of the only thing changing being how far and what direction I have to walk in. As mentioned upgrades just let you:[list] [*]Do things easier (sprint longer, hang more tickets, scan more tickets, carry an extra item, whatever) [*]Increase how long it takes for your cat to have a meltie because you were out of the room (honestly like 75% of the upgrades are random cat things) [*]Refill your cat's meltdown meter [*]Unlock new areas the next day[/list] In all this game is impressively shallow and easily mastered within thirty minutes, content exhausted within 100 (the ending is just white text on a black background by the way). The only thing it has going for it is the relatively low price tag of 9$, but there's certainly more interesting games that could hold your attention for much longer even at similar price points.

Man, this was a strange one. This is probably the first time I've been able to say "if you've played the demo, then you've played the full release." The only *significant* difference between the demo and the full release is that the full release is longer :\ The mechanics you experience in the demo are the exact same mechanics you experience in the full release. Nothing new is introduced. Sure the full release has more items/upgrades to purchase, but all they do is serve to stretch out the play time. There are no significant differences, mechanic-wise, that separates it from the Demo. The game can last you anywhere from 2-3 hours, but due to the lack of anything evolving throughout the game, the gameplay-loop far overstays its welcome and gets repetitive fast. I feel the game should have ended around the half-way mark. As for specifics, there really is no story to speak of; the cat plays no more of a significant role in the full release—still just a glorified count-down timer; nothing changes ability-wise with the monsters roaming the building; and nothing changes about your character that changes up the gameplay loop. The only thing that *does* change throughout the game are the locations in which the gameplay loop takes place. So, in the beginning Warehouse, the game allows you to get familiar with the few mechanics it does have. However, once you've learned them, which takes maybe 15-20 min, you've learned everything you'll need to know for the rest of the game. The game then opens up to a new location, Basement 1, where you repeat everything you were doing in the Warehouse, but now you're in the Basement 1 area. Then when you're done with the Basement 1 area, you then go repeat everything you've *been* doing, but in the Basement 2 area. Then when that area is complete, you just do it all again, but in the HR area. Absolutely nothing changes other than the locations, which is disappointing because I felt like this game had some potential :\ The game isn't terrible, but I was definitely hoping for more. The game *is* fun, but the fun lasts while the gameplay loop is still new. Unfortunately, the lack of variety in the gameplay loop becomes painfully apparent the longer you play. Not terrible, not great. Pretty mediocre. Game should have ended around the halfway point. Game should be cheaper.

还在痛苦的小伙伴看过来，攻略要点：（亮度调最高） 一、B1F： 1.Day1是不会有高能的，买个手电熟悉了货架摆放逻辑，重新开，一路跑，系统不会刷第二、第三排，货架争取第一天能送达$250以上； 2.Day2高能出现，250元，买150元跑鞋、3格摆放架，争取250元，请使用手机或截图拿货，解锁第二排货架； 3.Day3买大背包，其余经费全买猫家具，前3天一律不买猫粮，猫条到500左右就很舒服了，这天也解锁第三排货架； 二、B-1F： 4.Day4疯狂割草，出120元B-1F门票，其余经费买猫家具，负一层高能强度等同于负二层高能强度，刚解锁请务必熟货架位置，特别要牢记出入口附近的下蹲双通货架，以及负二层入口至负一层两个出口的路线，能跑不引到高能为最优； 5.Day5还是负一层割草，准备负二层门票及5格拉条，猫家具照常买； 6.Day6如果猫家具没买满请务必买满，买满的话直接下负二层。负一层高能听力、光敏感度、爆点高能声音敏感度都比一层高能强了一个档次，绕行过程中请保证你跟高能中间有视野遮挡物； 三、B-2F： 7.Day7最好能进这张图，区域分左右半场，下楼层前请规划半场路线，左右来回晃非常浪费时间，而且这层地形不好的货柜货物就不要拿了，空格货架以及底层格子满载情况非常常见，溜保安非常不好溜； 8.Day8，攒够800大洋出HR层门票，猫家具拉满； 四、HR层（真“人力”资源，其实Day3解锁的一层K、L货架就已经刷“人力”资源了） 9.Day9，期待的HR层解锁了，真是白给层，没啥难点，给再强的高能都没用，门口电脑给当天随机出门码，在一层左侧仓库门按密码即可通关！ 总结： 其实转化下视角，玩起来会有新的体验：玩家扮演仓库神偷，仓库中央的房间已经被玩家渗透为基地，物流输运设备是销赃设备，玩家需要潜入有“超能”看守的仓库，趁其不备拿走高价值货物返回临时潜入点销赃，玩家的猫咪则扮演放哨人的角色，玩家必须在放哨条时间耗尽前，顺到指定金额的货物并安全返回潜入基地。 游戏中的“高能”则扮演仓库保安的角色，虽然有千里眼加持，且速度比小偷强，能高速冲刺一击必杀，但无奈巡逻速度实在太慢，究其原因竟是无良老板不给保安配鞋，赤脚走路确实吧唧声大！ 最后是Day1即可通关的邪道攻略：拿个箱子（放不放泡沫的无所谓）封口，在门口货架处，视角拉最低，左键用箱子垫jio，然后起飞，俯瞰地图，从仓库侧门摔落，通关退款！（碰撞体积能起飞，怪也可以，我用了20多个箱子把1层高能挤飞了，然后系统又刷新位置，不如自己起飞）

[h2][b]猫好，人好，货物坏！[/b][/h2] 刚发售的时候我承认我是被这个接地气的游戏名字吸引到的...英文Order13，以为又是一个国外开发商拿中文互联网梗蹭热度的游戏，进页面发现是个恐怖独游遂买之，体验过游戏后没想到这个名字挺合适啊 玩家扮演的是一个要钱不要命的发货员，所需要做的就是接单、找货柜、拿货、途中再和怪物打个心理战，选择和绕它还是躲它，这期间还要注意你的猫猫好感度会随时间下降，确保每日都有剩余的钱留给猫买猫粮，猫相当于有限的取货时间，每天完成订单额度后可以买道具提升游戏体验，比如手电 扫码机 背包 跑鞋（帮助记忆密码、多带一格货）每一个道具都相当于降低难度，当然成就里面有不买道具通关的，如果玩家不借助外部手段的话还是挺有挑战的，[spoiler]无扫码机可以屏幕截图、无手电可以拉高屏幕亮度[/spoiler]，想挑战自我的也能打个两三周目吧，最近也更新了佛系模式即无怪物无JumpScare，真成送货模拟器了呗 游戏分为四个区域，需要玩家攒钱买区域通行证才能通过，花费和难度也逐级递增，第一个区域也就是最简单的，货架都按顺序排列，无非是要绕绕路，无手电无背包无扫码机都可以打得过的。第二第三个区域地下室B1和B2就有不少惊吓点，货架摆放的也不规则了，记住位置的同时也要注意怪物，特别是B2在一个完全渗水而且没有光线的货舱，就是最后恐怖的区域了，再最后是HR人力资源部，进去你就知道为什么叫human resources了，就是你最终要送的货物[spoiler]正常订单里夹杂着人体残肢的单子[/spoiler]，当然也可以不送，里面拿到紧急出口密码就能通关了，感觉这个设定和氛围做大一点能像史丹利寓言那样的[spoiler]一步步揭示公司不为人知的秘密[/spoiler]，但就是一小体量的恐怖独游，开发商最近也有在更新而且UI和场景都有中文值得一试

猫好，货坏，人快，鬼菜！ 【对方向感差的人不太友好，但是如果你方向感不错一定要尝试。】 确实有意思，它的货架位置固定，但是档你的东西会随机刷(被抓后)。3个小时前的意犹未尽，3-5个小时之后，食之无味，弃之可惜，真的很难过。希望续作能给更多游戏性，或着在本体的基础上出些DLC，新图，更多的机制，新的怪，更充实的游戏性。 建议： 我觉得 定价&游戏时长 不是很合理，要增加游戏性和时长，可以尝试把东西价格分级话，然后设置难度，不同的难度设置不同的价格。佛系依旧保持，为：佛系，目前的价格和怪为: 入门。增高商品售价/降低订单价格/修改订单目标，第3-5天开始卡比极限值低1趟左右的目标订单价值，为：正常。其余参数不动，每天都卡极限值，为：困难。什么装备都不买，而且赚到的钱只够缓慢升级猫咪幸福度，每天都是卡极限值，为地狱。这游戏性嘎嘎直接拉到20个小时左右。 喜欢的点：游戏优化比普通模拟器游戏好，细节等等都是费了很多心思在做的，非常nice。猫咪很可爱。流程和教学很有意思，感觉跟玩VR一样。 最后：祝贵司大卖~

ORDER 13 follows a simple gameplay loop: 1. Get orders at the safehouse 2. Leave safehouse and find order items (while avoiding wandering monsters) 3. Make your way back to safehouse 4. Package and ship orders for money to meet a daily quota Then after each day, you'll rack up more money that you can use for upgrades. Now don't get me wrong, I can totally see how this game might appeal to other people, but I personally found it more frustrating than enjoyable. While the game does have an interesting gameplay loop, it gets boring a little too fast even with the many purchasable item upgrades. My biggest complaint, however, are the monsters. These ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things are infuriating through and through, especially during the mid-game section. You'll be trapped in a room with tight spaces and you'll start to notice the visual cones are noticeably more inconsistent as if they have eyes in the back of their heads. I should be able to stealth around these creatures instead of having to worry about one of them randomly activating their sixth sense to ♥♥♥♥ me out of nowhere. In my opinion, this game would have been great if there was a better way to defend yourself because hiding and waiting for them to walk away gets old and annoying super fast. This game might not be for me, but I would still recommend trying it out, especially when its on sale so that you can make your own judgement call. Overall, although ORDER 13 does have a nice concept, it unfortunately just fell flat for me.

Gather packages from the right shelve in a large warehouse, pack them correctly and put them on the delivery band. It's one of those boring nine to five jobs. Luckily your cat is keeping you company. I say luckily, but the bugger is a bit demanding. Don't stay away for too long or it will end badly. For you. Oh and there are monsters creeping around in the dark. And they are hungry! it's a neat little game. Mechanics are simple: complete orders to get money, buy upgrades from money, unlock new areas of the warehouse with higher rewards and try to survive another day. The audio makes it quite tense, not just the sounds from the monsters themselves. Use headphones with proper 3d audio output.
It was cute! (the cat) It was scary! It was stressful... But after all...It was fun! Totally recommend!

No story, no lore, just a work simulator. There seems to be only one kind of monster. There are some "scary things" statically scattered in the warehouse (some bodies and body parts) and random noises. There are no notably special events or unforseeable things or anything, which could have made this game kind of interesting. Absolutly nothing of it, so game for me was absolutely boring. The basic game idea is great, but implementation is absolute wasted potential. Exellent examples of a work simulators with horror vibe are for me "the mortuary assistant", "cabin factory" and maybe "the bathhouse". The only good thing is that you can deactivate the monsters and the cat issues you you do not like to be stressed at work. Technically, the game was ok, i found no bugs, performance was ok, graphics and sound nice and controls felt good. But not my kind of game. One additional point is criticism: the trailer suggested some voice output, but there wasn't one spoken line, but I only played till day 5 or so.
